title: Shimon Efrati
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman relates in connection with [Ketubot 103a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.103a.25) that Rabbi, before his death, said: “Yosef Chafni and Shimon Efrati served me in my life, and they will serve me in my death.” It was thought that they would attend to his burial. Later it became apparent that they had died before Rabbi, and his meaning was understood: they would serve him there.[^1][^2]
Hyman says that in [Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 12:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Ketubot.12.3.3), he is called Yosef Efrati.[^3]

notes.text: Hyman’s print (vol. III, pp. 1155–1156) has 103a, where the linked Bavli passage appears. The supplied Hebrew reads 103b.

The [Bavli’s continuation](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.103a.31) says that their biers preceded Rabbi’s, clarifying why his instruction was understood to refer to the next world. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3451&lang=en) records Shimon Efrati and Yosef Chafni as attendants of Rabbi.

Hyman’s print and the supplied Hebrew give the Yerushalmi locator as chapter 2, halakhah 3. The linked parallel is at 12:3. Its Hebrew has Yosef Efrati and Yoseh Chafni, whereas its English gives Yose Ephrati and Joseph from Haifa.
